stories.title: CBI court acquits CPI(M) leaders in Shukkoor murder case
stories.summary: A CBI Special Court acquitted CPI(M) leaders P. Jayarajan and T.V. Rajesh in the murder case of IUML worker Abdul Shukkoor. While the court found 13 other individuals guilty, 16 additional accused were also acquitted alongside the two party leaders. The case remains a matter of political significance.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi calls Indian democracy sacred at University of Chicago
stories.summary: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi told students at the University of Chicago that Indian democracy is sacred. He stated that boycotting elections would end the system and that the Congress party requires absolute proof before claiming the electoral process is flawed. The system remains under discussion.

stories.title: Shiv Sena members protest Sonia Gandhi memoir
stories.summary: Shiv Sena members tore pages from Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging, citing objectionable references to Vinayak Damodar Savarkar. The party has demanded that publisher Harper Collins scrap the pages and requested a state-wide ban in Maharashtra. The publisher has yet to comment on the requested edits.

stories.title: Supreme Court declines to stay Azam Khan bail
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to intervene in the interim bail granted to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan by the Allahabad High Court. The ED had challenged the release, citing financial irregularities at Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The court noted that the High Court order will not influence final proceedings.

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav alleges injustice against Dalits in Gorakhpur
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav claimed that Dalits in Gorakhpur face significant injustice. He predicted a double-zero defeat for the BJP on the Chief Minister's home turf if elections were held today. He described the upcoming assembly election as a necessary effort to save the state's democracy.

stories.title: Bhajan Lal Sharma faces shifting criticism as CM
stories.summary: Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma is nearing his three-year term. Initially dismissed by Congress state president Govind Singh Dotasara as a Parchi CM chosen by central leadership, he is now accused by the same critic of having finished off the BJP in the state entirely.

stories.title: INDIA bloc questions Election Commission over electoral rolls
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is considering a request from INDIA bloc leaders to submit 48 interrogatories to the Election Commission. The questions challenge the nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, seeking to determine if the Commission acted collectively and how the exercise was authorized by the governing body.

stories.title: Tejashwi Yadav labels Bihar minister a fake
stories.summary: Tejashwi Yadav accused Bihar Minister Ashok Choudhary of illegally holding three positions simultaneously, including his ministerial role and a university lecturing post. The controversy follows a finding by the Bihar Lok Bhawan that the teaching position violates office-of-profit provisions. The minister has not resigned from his posts.

stories.title: Tripura court orders FIR against Minister Tinku Roy
stories.summary: A Tripura court directed police to register a complaint against Minister Tinku Roy for allegedly submitting false information in his 2023 election affidavit. The order follows a failure by local police to initiate an investigation after the initial complaint was lodged at the Kailashahar police station.

stories.title: Activist seeks equal election symbol access
stories.summary: Social activist Amitabh Thakur has petitioned the Election Commission to reconsider the exclusive reservation of election symbols for recognized parties. He argues that current rules create a structural disadvantage for independent candidates and unrecognized parties by denying them the lasting voter familiarity afforded to established political organizations.

stories.title: SP and Congress to discuss UP seat-sharing after November 20
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav stated that seat-sharing negotiations with Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections will begin after November 20. The parties aim to balance candidate winnability against seat counts in the 403-seat assembly, where the BJP remains the primary electoral opponent.

stories.title: Azam Khan released on interim bail
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was released from Dasna jail following a Supreme Court decision not to stay his interim bail in a money laundering case. The court will continue to hear the Enforcement Directorate's challenge to the High Court order that originally granted the relief.

stories.title: Odisha evacuates over one lakh as Cyclone Akvan nears
stories.summary: Odisha has evacuated over one lakh people, including 10,000 pregnant women, ahead of the expected landfall of Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan near Gopalpur. Disaster response forces are positioned across southern and coastal districts. The storm is projected to cross the state coast by noon on November 20.

stories.title: CID arrests man in seven crore job fraud case
stories.summary: The CID has arrested a 50-year-old man, Nimmakayala Peddiraju, for allegedly cheating job aspirants of seven crore rupees. The scheme promised government employment to unemployed youth. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the suspect and his associates involved in the collection of funds.

stories.title: Bus accident in Anantapur leaves 40 injured
stories.summary: A private bus traveling from Bengaluru to Hyderabad overturned near Raptadu in Anantapur, injuring at least 40 passengers. The driver fled the scene after the vehicle veered off the road. Officials reported that the injured passengers are in stable condition at nearby hospitals.

stories.title: ASI waives monument entry fees for Heritage Week
stories.summary: The Archaeological Survey of India has waived entry fees for all centrally protected monuments, including the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort, on November 19. The move marks the start of World Heritage Week, which runs through November 25, to encourage public awareness of heritage conservation.

stories.title: Telangana records season low of 11 degrees Celsius
stories.summary: Temperatures in Telangana dropped to a season low of 11 degrees Celsius in Kumaram Bheem Asifabad on the night of November 18. Other districts also reported temperatures near 11 degrees, according to the Telangana Development Planning Society. Hyderabad recorded a relatively warmer 16.5 degrees.

stories.title: Six killed as car plunges into Bihar canal
stories.summary: Six people, including three minors, died when their car fell into a canal in Bihar's Araria district on Wednesday night. One survivor is currently undergoing treatment at a local hospital. Police stated the driver lost control of the vehicle while crossing the Bidi bridge.

stories.title: BMC demolishes building linked to Dawood Ibrahim
stories.summary: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation has begun razing a south Mumbai building formerly used by Dawood Ibrahim. The structure was classified as C-1, a designation for buildings deemed dangerous. The demolition proceeded under police security, with the site obscured by blue tin sheets.

stories.title: Tensions rise at Kolkata Medical College after student protest
stories.summary: Junior doctors at Medical College, Kolkata, gheraoed the principal to protest show-cause notices issued after a recent stampede. Following the protest, outsiders attacked students and damaged property. Students blamed the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, which has denied involvement in the incident.

stories.title: IAF displays fleet readiness in Hakimpet
stories.summary: The Indian Air Force Helicopter Training School at Hakimpet recently achieved 100 percent serviceability, flying all 23 helicopters in a single coordinated display. The school says this demonstrates maintenance excellence and crew coordination. All aircraft were fit to fly simultaneously.

stories.title: Census 2027 portal updates religion list
stories.summary: The 2027 Census self-enumeration portal now uses predictive text for 76 "Other" religion entries. This follows the removal of over 200 options, including ISKCON and Sanatan, which were previously available in a drop-down menu. The government updated the list on the day the portal launched.

stories.title: Man arrested after rape of minor in Greater Noida
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man was arrested following an exchange of fire with police after allegedly raping a 13-year-old girl in Badalpur village. Police stated the suspect lured the student to an agricultural field under the pretext of work before assaulting her.

stories.title: Three killed in house fire in Shamli
stories.summary: A 32-year-old woman and her two daughters, aged 11 and 13, died in a house fire in Kaidi village late Wednesday. Officials suspect an LPG cylinder blast caused the blaze, though the exact cause remains under investigation.

stories.title: Rail Parcel App to launch in eight cities
stories.summary: The Ministry of Railways is rolling out the Rail Parcel App to provide doorstep parcel booking and delivery services. The digital platform will debut in Hyderabad and seven other major cities. The service aims to modernize logistics through end-to-end digital transactions.

stories.title: Two arrested in PayU cloud server fraud
stories.summary: Gurugram police arrested two men from Ludhiana for allegedly facilitating a cyber fraud involving a breach of PayU cloud servers. The suspects reportedly provided bank accounts to criminals who siphoned over 25 crore rupees from the payments provider.

stories.title: Two arrested in PayU cloud server breach
stories.summary: Gurugram police have arrested two individuals from Ludhiana in connection with a 25.67 crore rupee fraud. The suspects allegedly provided bank accounts used to siphon funds after cybercriminals gained unauthorized access to PayU Payments cloud servers.

stories.title: SpiceJet board approves 5,500 crore rupee fundraising
stories.summary: SpiceJet's board has approved a plan to raise up to 5,500 crore rupees through fresh shares or other financial instruments. The airline intends to use the capital to strengthen its financial position and support revival plans. The proposal remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

stories.title: A2B secures 180 million dollar investment
stories.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan has secured 180 million dollars from Bodhi Tree Systems, a firm backed by James Murdoch and Uday Shankar. The 50-year-old brand sold a majority stake in the deal. The funds are intended for expansion into new markets.

stories.title: Sub-panel to review Arunachal hydroelectric project
stories.summary: A sub-committee will assess the environmental and social impact of the 1720 MW Kamala Hydroelectric Project in Arunachal Pradesh. The proposal requires diverting over 3,200 hectares of forest land and involves felling 2.34 million trees and bamboo.

stories.title: Delhi traffic police seize 17,000 end-of-life vehicles
stories.summary: Delhi Traffic Police impounded over 17,000 vehicles between January and November 2, citing their status as end-of-life. The majority were two-wheelers. Authorities launched an awareness drive to encourage owners to surrender older vehicles for authorized scrapping.

stories.title: Elephant linked to 16 deaths tranquilized
stories.summary: An elephant blamed for 16 human deaths in Chhattisgarh has been tranquilized and fitted with a satellite radio collar. Forest personnel tracked the animal for months before the operation. The elephant was released back into the forest following the procedure.

stories.title: India addresses historical emissions at COP31
stories.summary: Environment minister Bhupender Yadav told the COP31 conference that the Global South should not bear the burden of historical emissions. He stated that climate action must be rooted in equity and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.

stories.title: Anbumani Ramadoss calls for wetland notification
stories.summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has urged the Tamil Nadu government to notify all state wetlands by January. He also demanded a halt to construction work, including a compound wall and walkway, currently underway near the Pallikaranai marshland.

stories.title: Chennai corporation issues de-occupation notices
stories.summary: The Greater Chennai Corporation has issued 124 de-occupation notices to coastal buildings with major planning violations. The move follows a High Court order regarding unauthorized construction and deviations from Coastal Regulation Zone norms.

stories.title: Madras HC mandates cattle licensing in urban areas
stories.summary: The Madras High Court has ordered mandatory licensing and tagging for cattle in urban Tamil Nadu. The ruling aims to prevent motor accidents caused by loose animals. Civic bodies must now enforce these measures to hold owners accountable.

stories.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
stories.summary: India and Canada may announce a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit in December, according to High Commissioner Dinesh K. Patnaik. Both nations are also finalising a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement. Mr. Patnaik noted that both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail mutual interests.

stories.title: PM Modi meets Prince and Princess of Wales, discusses boosting U.K.-India ties
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Prince William and Princess Catherine in New Delhi to discuss the India-U.K. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The meeting focused on defence and health cooperation, building on the India-U.K. Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement that entered into force in July. The Prince and Princess remain busy.

stories.title: Pakistan Minister to lead delegation to Delhi for SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
stories.summary: Federal Minister for Climate Change Dr. Musadik Masood Malik will lead a Pakistani delegation to the SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. The visit follows an invitation from the Union Ministry of Culture and Tourism to discuss civilisational dialogue and diplomacy.

stories.title: India-US ties at historic high, working towards fair, reciprocal trade relationship: US envoy
stories.summary: US Deputy Chief of Mission Jason Meeks stated that India-US relations are at a historic high, with both governments working to build a fair and reciprocal trade relationship. Speaking at the 23rd Indo-US Economic Summit, Meeks called for reduced trade barriers and improved supply chain resilience between the nations.

stories.title: ‘Misuse discussion for propaganda’: India slams Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
stories.summary: India’s UN representative Parvathaneni Harish criticised the Pakistani delegation for raising the Indus Waters Treaty at a Security Council meeting. India accused the Pakistani military of looting natural resources for personal gain and triggering domestic political turmoil to maintain control. The meeting was convened to discuss resources and conflict.

stories.title: Malaysia to end visa-free entry for Indians from January 1, 2027
stories.summary: Malaysia will withdraw its visa-free entry facility for Indian nationals starting January 1, 2027. The Immigration Department of Malaysia announced that all Indian travellers must obtain a visa before arrival. Visa applications through the MyVISA online portal will open for Indian passport holders on December 1, 2026.

stories.title: Trusted India-Japan partnership vital amid global uncertainty, says Jaishankar
stories.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar told the inaugural Raisina Tokyo event that an expansion of India-Japan ties will stabilise the Indo-Pacific. Jaishankar stated that trusted partnerships are a solution to global uncertainty, as most countries move to de-risk and diversify their economic interests in an increasingly multipolar Asia.

stories.title: Rajnath Singh says India-Japan maritime ties key to free, open Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated that maritime cooperation between India and Japan reflects deep trust and a shared commitment to regional security. Singh noted that the partnership aims to realise a free and open Indo-Pacific based on the rule of law, following his recent remarks on X.

stories.title: Malaysia to not remain visa free for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027
stories.summary: Malaysia will end its visa-free policy for Indian visitors on January 1, 2027, citing an increase in individuals using the 30-day facility to seek employment. The High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur warned that such activity constitutes a clear violation of immigration rules. Tourism was the original goal.

stories.title: PM Modi jumps on GTA VI craze, posts about India’s ‘level up’ since GTA V
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to highlight India’s development since the 2013 launch of GTA V. Posting on X, the Prime Minister shared graphics comparing national progress to the game’s timeline, stating that India is now playing a whole new game.

stories.title: Indian-American executive Jay Puri oversaw Nvidia chip sales to Alice Huang: Report
stories.summary: Nvidia executive Jay Puri oversaw chip sales to Alice Huang, who US intelligence agencies reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset, according to The Information. Puri, 71, has led Nvidia’s global sales operations since 2005. The report details his involvement in the company’s business ties to China.

stories.title: 'India playing a whole new game': Modi invokes GTA 6 to highlight transformation
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI to compare India’s development since the 2013 release of GTA V. The Prime Minister presented a series of slides on social media to frame national upgrades as a scoreboard, noting that India has transformed during the game's development.

stories.title: Bigger than any movie, ever: Grand Theft Auto VI arrives in record-shattering media release
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launched globally on Wednesday following an eight-year development cycle. The game, a sequel to a title that sold over 220 million copies, reportedly earned more revenue than any film in history before consoles even began booting the software. The entertainment industry has a new benchmark.

stories.title: GTA 6 goes live in India after 13-year wait
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI officially launched in India at midnight on Thursday, ending a 13-year wait since the release of GTA V. Players who pre-ordered the digital version were able to download the game in advance, though access remained locked until the official release time across all regions.

stories.title: ‘GTA 6 has a Bengaluru connection’: Tejasvi Surya highlights 1,600 developers' hard work
stories.summary: BJP MP Tejasvi Surya stated that over 1,600 developers at Rockstar India in Bengaluru contributed to the development of Grand Theft Auto VI. Surya highlighted the city's role in the project as the game’s global release approached, noting the significant effort involved in creating the highly anticipated title.

stories.title: GTA 6 India release time: Indians await much-anticipated game as New Zealand gets to play
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for release in India at midnight on November 19, 2026. Rockstar Games confirmed the launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X S platforms. Indian gamers will access the title at the same local time as other regions following the global rollout.

stories.title: "India Playing Whole New Game": PM Modi's GTA-Style Dig At Opposition
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s social media post comparing India’s development to the release cycle of the Grand Theft Auto video game series has gone viral. The post utilised the game's visual themes to frame the current administration's performance against the tenure of the previous government.

stories.title: Console, Internet, Hardware: Why Playing GTA 6 Feels Like Luxury
stories.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on Thursday, marking the end of a 13-year wait for the next mainline entry in the series. The release has prompted discussions regarding the hardware and connectivity requirements necessary to play the game, which is now available on current-generation consoles.

stories.title: Modi compares India to GTA 6
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI to highlight India's economic and infrastructure transformation over the last 13 years. Sharing graphics styled after the game, he stated that India is playing a whole new game. The country has reached a new level.

stories.title: Rockstar India studio worked on GTA 6
stories.summary: BJP leader Tejasvi Surya said that Rockstar India's Bengaluru studio contributed significantly to the development of Grand Theft Auto VI. Surya noted that more than 1,600 developers in the city worked on the game. The upcoming release has a local connection.

stories.title: GTA 6 release triggers wider commercial ripple effects
stories.summary: The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to become one of the largest entertainment releases in history. While Take-Two Interactive benefits from game sales, the release is creating commercial opportunities across food delivery, music streaming, and merchandise. The industry is competing for consumer time.

stories.title: Ukraine damages Kerch Bridge
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces used drones and missiles to bring down a span of the road bridge and damage the rail bridge at the Kerch crossing. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the event an unprecedented operation. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage to the structure previously described as a miracle.

stories.title: India criticizes Pakistan at UN
stories.summary: India accused the Pakistani military of looting natural resources and triggering political turmoil to maintain control. The remarks came during a UN Security Council meeting on natural resources and conflict. India stated it had no intention to discuss bilateral disputes but would not remain silent.

stories.title: Pakistan mining deal involves US billionaire and Chinese firms
stories.summary: A new mining venture in Balochistan links Chinese state-owned firms to billionaire Robert Friedland and the Pakistan Army-backed Fauji Foundation. Friedland's company, I-Pulse, recently received a $250 million US government grant. The deal aims for greenfield exploration across highly prospective licenses in the province.

stories.title: Muslim population projected to grow
stories.summary: Projections indicate that the global religious landscape will shift by 2070. While India's Hindu population is expected to increase, its share of the total population will likely decline. Muslims are expected to become the world's largest religious group by 2035, overtaking Christians.

stories.title: Heart valve procedure performed on 80-year-old
stories.summary: Doctors at Sri Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research treated an 80-year-old woman for mitral valve leakage using a minimally invasive MitraClip procedure. The patient had previously undergone open-heart surgery. The hospital avoided a high-risk operation by using the new device.

stories.title: Doctor reduces rare disease drug cost
stories.summary: A Hyderabad-based paediatrician has lowered the cost of a rare disease drug from 9 crore rupees to 2.5 lakh rupees. Seven children with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome will receive a year of treatment for free. The initiative aims to improve access to the medicine tiratricol.

stories.title: Assam medical college withdraws marriage deferral order
stories.summary: The Department of Medicine at Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an order advising postgraduate trainees to defer marriage until their residency ended. The head of the department rescinded the directive hours after it was issued, following a backlash from a doctors' body.

stories.title: Health ministry proposes antimicrobial oversight
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed including antimicrobials under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules. The amendment aims to strengthen oversight of quality and safety to address antimicrobial resistance. The ministry is seeking to include these drugs in the central regulatory framework.

stories.title: Assam medical college rescinds marriage advice
stories.summary: A department at Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an order asking postgraduate trainees to postpone personal milestones like marriage during their residency. The directive sparked controversy shortly after its release. The National Medical Commission regulations allow for maternity and paternity leave for students.

stories.title: ICMR launches infectious disease surveillance network
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has launched a syndromic surveillance initiative to provide early warnings for disease outbreaks. The network will use real-time health data across 70 laboratories to provide feedback for epidemiological investigations. The scheme is part of the department of health research.

stories.title: Students hospitalised after pollution incident
stories.summary: Sixty-two students were hospitalised in Kerala following reports of thick smoke and a pungent smell from a nearby tar-mixing plant. The students experienced nausea and breathing difficulties. Authorities reported that all affected individuals are currently stable.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu to implement HPV-DNA testing
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government will implement HPV-DNA testing for cervical cancer in five districts. The first phase of the programme aims to cover over 124,000 women. The initiative follows an announcement made by the Chief Minister earlier this year.

stories.title: Opposition flags healthcare crisis in Attappady
stories.summary: Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan alleged that the healthcare system in Attappady has collapsed. Citing a shortage of doctors and the suspension of scanning services, he called for protests against government policies. He requested 5 lakh rupees in compensation for each infant death in the region.

stories.title: Students hospitalised in Kerala
stories.summary: Sixty-two students from Auxilium ISC School were hospitalised after complaining of nausea and breathing difficulties. Local authorities suspect pollution from a nearby tar-mixing unit caused the incident. Police stated that none of the students suffered major health issues and all remain stable.

stories.title: Agricultural university receives A grade
stories.summary: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University has been awarded an A grade by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research. The university previously held a B grade. The accreditation, which follows improvements in research and education, is valid through March 2031.

stories.title: Investigation into Air India crash that killed 260 in final stage
stories.summary: The Indian government told the Supreme Court on Wednesday that the investigation into last year's Air India crash is in its final stage. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta requested a three week adjournment to follow global protocols. The court is currently hearing a petition for an independent probe.

stories.title: Kerala University team secures patent for solar-active hydrogen material
stories.summary: A research team from Kerala University has received an Indian patent for a spinel ferrite-based photocatalyst designed for hydrogen production. The university says the invention absorbs a broad spectrum of solar radiation from ultraviolet to near-infrared. It is described as an achievement in nanoscience and sustainable energy research.

stories.title: Chikkanna discusses transition from comedian to lead actor
stories.summary: Kannada comedian Chikkanna is awaiting the November 27 release of his second film as a lead actor, Lakshmiputhra. The actor, who debuted as a hero in 2023, is currently discussing his career shift and his experiences working with Yash. The transition from comedy to lead roles remains a challenge.

stories.title: Bengaluru studio launches rhythm platformer game
stories.summary: Tathvamasi Studios has released Suri: The Seventh Note, a 2D rhythm platformer where the environment moves in tune with a corrupted musical presence. The game, directed by founder Glen Martin, follows a protagonist attempting to save her mother. It is now available on Steam and the Playstation Store.

stories.title: Prince William's ancestry discussed
Historical profile of Tiwari Haata in Uttar Pradesh
Career path of DCP Rajiv Kumar
South Korea implements strict rules for college entrance exams
stories.summary: South Korea has introduced new regulations for its high-stakes college entrance exams, including heightened scrutiny of student attire. The measures follow concerns over potential AI-assisted cheating. Some students report that the new rules and the surrounding scandal have increased their anxiety levels during the testing period.

stories.title: Ahmedabad police issue warning ahead of Diljit Dosanjh concert
stories.summary: Ahmedabad police have issued a public warning regarding conduct ahead of a scheduled concert by Diljit Dosanjh. The artist shared the official notice on his Instagram account. The warning follows a series of local security measures intended to manage the event.

stories.title: Wedding of Kavya Maran and Anirudh Ravichander sparks political discussion
stories.summary: The marriage of Sun Group heiress Kavya Maran to composer Anirudh Ravichander has prompted public debate regarding Dravidian politics. Observers are questioning whether the movement has shifted from the inter-caste reformist alliances of the 1960s toward a traditional accommodation. The family has noted a history of similar marriages.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi recounts visit to Cambridge restaurant
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi recently visited the Varsity Restaurant in Cambridge, a location associated with his parents, Sonia and Rajiv. Gandhi noted that while his parents remembered the venue fondly, they recalled the food as being poor. He advised others to avoid the chicken while visiting the establishment.
